title: Shadoof
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the page 56 shadoof has a pivoted beam, a hanging bucket, an opposing counterweight and a water tray. Lower uses an external hand to push the bucket down against the counterweight. Fill immerses the bucket and admits water. Raise uses a light hand input with counterweight assistance to lift the full bucket. See-through exposes the beam pivot, suspension, bucket and counterweight attachments. Lever arms and opposing moments are overlays. Identify the tray and external water refill as teaching fixtures. Do not add a motor, valve train or pulley to reach a part count.
blurb: A scale teaching adaptation of the shadoof lever, with a human hand, counterweight assistance and an external water tray reset.
adaptationNotes: Teaching base, tray and external refill jug are fixtures.
The person tips the raised bucket back into the tray as a teaching water reset.
Dashed lever arms and opposing moment arrows are overlays, not anatomy.
Motion is slowed and prescribed by human input, with a counterweight assisting the filled bucket lift.
This is a water-lifting lever, not a pulley or a perpetual pumping cycle.
A second external hand lifts and tips the refill jug. The falling stream transfers jug water into the tray. A hand also tips the bucket during the teaching reset.
